name: Hall of Explorers
summary: The Hall of Explorers is the sprawling archaeological wing of Ironforge and the bustling headquarters of the dwarven Explorers' League. Part museum, part archive, and part expedition command, it gathers relics, fossils, and ancient tomes from every corner of Azeroth to piece together the forgotten origins of the dwarven race.

sections.title: Headquarters of the League
sections.body: Occupying the northeastern cavern of Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers—sometimes referred to as the Assembly of Explorers—serves as the nerve center for all Alliance-sanctioned archaeological endeavors. Under the direction of High Explorer Muninn Magellas, scholars and field agents coordinate digs across distant lands, shipping back mysterious relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. The vast Library at its center functions as both a public museum and a restricted storehouse of historical lore.

faq.q: What is the Hall of Explorers used for?
faq.answer: It serves as the global headquarters and archival museum of the Explorers' League. Scholars analyze field reports, catalog relics from excavations, and organize archaeological digs to uncover the origins of the dwarves and ancient Azeroth.
High Explorer Muninn Magellas oversees the hall's expeditions, museum curation, and research archives from within the district.

faq.q: How does this place connect to the rest of Ironforge?
faq.answer: The Hall of Explorers lies in the northeastern section of the city. Archways connect it directly to the Great Forge to the southwest, the Forlorn Cavern to the west, and Tinker Town to the south.

angles.text: For dwarven adventurers, the hall is the ultimate repository of your race's heritage, housing relics aimed at uncovering your ancient origins and connection to the Titans.
